# OEIS draft — staged 2026-06-02. Submit via https://oeis.org (needs a human account).
# Verify all terms first with:  node count.mjs        (reproduces 0,0,1,44 and the
# calibration values 44 = truncated octahedron, 5396/10792 = minimus extents).

%S 0,0,1,44
%N Number of undirected Hamiltonian cycles in the Cayley graph of the symmetric group S_n generated by the n-1 adjacent transpositions s_i = (i,i+1); equivalently, the number of Hamiltonian cycles in the 1-skeleton of the n-permutohedron.
%C The graph has n! vertices (the permutations of n elements) and is (n-1)-regular; two permutations are adjacent when one is obtained from the other by a single adjacent transposition. For n=4 this graph is the truncated octahedron, so a(4) = 44 agrees with the truncated-octahedron entry of A343433.
%C This is the enumeration underlying English change ringing: an "extent" rings every row (permutation) exactly once and returns to rounds, which is exactly a Hamiltonian cycle here. See D. E. Knuth, TAOCP 4A, 7.2.1.2 ("Algorithm P: Plain changes"), and A. T. White, "Ringing the Cosets".
%C The directed count rooted at a fixed vertex is 2*a(n).
%C Sister graph: if a change may instead be any non-empty product of *disjoint* adjacent transpositions (the generating set actually used in change ringing; its degree is A000071(n+2) = Fibonacci(n+1)-1), the n=4 count is 5396 undirected = 10792 directed, the standard number of extents on minimus.
%C a(5) is the number of Hamiltonian cycles of the 120-vertex 5-permutohedron (the bubble-sort graph of S_5). Its exact value is open: brute-force enumeration is infeasible (the answer is ~10^21, too large to list; the backtracking search tree is ~5*10^23 nodes by Knuth random-dive estimation), and an exact frontier-based count (Simpath/ZDD) is set by the graph's vertex separation, for which the best edge ordering found here achieves 23 (an upper bound: 85M simulated-annealing iterations could not improve on it, and the achieving order was independently re-checked, but no lower-bound certificate is known to us): a disk-backed frontier sweep measured 2.55*10^9 distinct frontier states at edge 79 of 240 with the census still growing and the sweep's widest stretch (cut width >= 22, 78 edge-steps) just beginning, projecting a peak of 2*10^10-10^13 states per level - a research-scale computation comparable to the 6-cube Hamiltonian-cycle enumeration (Deza-Shklyar 2010, arXiv:1003.4391), not a large-memory workstation job. Sequential importance sampling, validated by recovering a(4)=44, estimates a(5) ~ 1.1 * 10^21 (95% CI 1.07-1.15 * 10^21; equal-weight pooled over 288 million dives across 48 independent seeds, with agreeing non-parametric-bootstrap and median-of-means cross-checks; the heavy-tailed estimator makes the interval indicative, not a bound). The validated engines (in-RAM and disk-backed/resumable) and the measured per-level state census are staged here. See the strata "The Extent" and "A Sextillion Ways Home".
%D D. E. Knuth, The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 4A, Section 7.2.1.2.
%H A. T. White, Ringing the Cosets, Amer. Math. Monthly 94 (1987), 721-746.
%e n=1,2: the graph has no cycle, so a(1)=a(2)=0. n=3: the graph is a hexagon, a(3)=1. n=4: the truncated octahedron has a(4)=44 Hamiltonian cycles.
%Y Cf. A343433 (Hamiltonian cycles of Archimedean solids; truncated octahedron term = 44), A324942 (change-ringing sequences on 4 bells; last term 10792), A000071 (number of legal changes = Fibonacci(n)-1), A057112.
%K nonn,more,hard,walk
%O 1,4
